page.layout: Running head at top right, page number at top left; one column of text, with a centred heading and a centred title below it; catchword at lower right; no margin notes.

main_text.p: Fluvius igitur antequam creverit, parvo obstaculo facilè declinatur in quamvis partem, quod obsta-culum ubi multum auctum fuerit, etsi nonnihil ex ea parte undas reflectat, statim tamen cum reliquo vasti fluminis pondere, cursum pristinum recipiunt.

Idem puta de vento qui tenuis in ortu, si verbi causa recta à Septentrione veniat, objecto monte, vel alicujus astri influxu facilè in dextram, aut finistram partem declinatur, ut jam fluctus ille sit collateralis.

Qui quidem flatus, ubi halituum copia in immensum creverit, nullo potest obice ab itinere coepto dimoveri, sed tantum densior factus per illas angustias fertur impetu vehementiori. Hinc sibila illa & stridores, mugitu'que ventorum, quoties ædificio, vel monte transverso, vel astro aliquo à latere influente, amnis ille halituum cogitur sese contrahere. Quin sicut montes celsi hinc inde flatum ejusmodi contrahunt: ita superne hinc inde Astrorum influxus multo magis eum potest comprimere. Qualis quidem astrorum influxio ventum non longè ab ortu suo adhuc tenuem facilè in hanc aut illam partem deflexisset, successu verò veluti in ingens mare auctum, etsi ab uno latere possit contrahere, tam vasti tamen æquoris impetum non potest aliò detorquere.
main_text.head: ARTICULUS XIII. Quare Terra viscera, fontiumque scaturigines, ac putei calidiores hyeme, & state sint frigidiores.
main_text.p: Hanc quæstionem huic loco visum est addere. Cur qui fontis, putei, locaque subterrena hybernis frigoribus fumant præ calore, æstivis caloribus valdè refrigescant. Toletus in lib. 1. de Generat. cap. 7. quæst. 14. ita nititur hunc nodum solvere.

page.notes: The first word of the article is a large drop-cap H; it is printed as one letter and is transcribed as "Hanc". The word "mugitu'que" is printed with an apostrophe; kept as printed. The catchword "Par-" is at lower right. Printed spellings such as "verò", "facilè", "longè" and "præ" are kept as printed. The word "solvere" was written as "soluere" in print; it is normalised here to the consonant v.
